provenance_note: Created 2026-08-26 from the Doctrine Mesh V2 separation-of-duties model, the Academic Extension Contract, and an entry/midflight role-completeness audit for this exact demonstration; corrected 2026-08-28 so a distinct meta-checker, not the completeness auditor, certifies each phase receipt.
reason_for_inclusion: Make research, rights, citation, claim-fidelity, graph, red-team, and completeness responsibilities explicit without pretending AI review is qualified human approval.

roles.purpose: Own the exact claimed paths, serialize edits, preserve gates, and assemble receipts.
At entry, midflight, and exit ask which specialist or checker is required, what concrete failure mode it closes, and whether later evidence revealed a missing role.

Independently replay each entry, midflight, and exit completeness audit; verify the auditor's role coverage, evidence, independence, path scope, and failure routing; and fail closed on self-attestation or aliased phase evidence.
knowledge_base_contract: adversarial fixture scope and reseal policy

roles.purpose: Find primary object/context records, excavation publications, critical editions, peer-reviewed alternatives, and limitations for bounded historical questions.
Separate physical witness, catalog metadata, image, transcription, edition, alignment, translation, and candidate-chunk states.
Verify exact asset identity, custodian, license scope, attribution, source URL, modification statement, and non-copyright caveats.
Open every public locator independently, distinguish source roles, test whether each claim is faithful to its sources, and search for material counterpositions.
Compare every public sentence and graph assertion with the cited source role, scope limit, uncertainty, and counterposition record.
Check identity, n-ary claim mediation, named-graph boundaries, source drift invalidation, extension preservation, and reverse blast-radius paths.
Try to construct forbidden artifact-to-Scripture, evidence-to-doctrine, direct-image-to-translation, or lower-trust-to-canonical paths.
Check public paths for secrets, private locators, unlicensed payloads, misleading completion claims, and immutable evidence consistency.
Route high-risk disagreement, architecture choices, qualified-expert requirements, doctrine questions, and promotion decisions to the named human authority.

selection_questions: What exact claim or transformation is being attempted?
Which knowledge boundary or failure mode is not covered by current roles?
Would the missing specialist materially change evidence selection, interpretation, or risk?
Can a primary source or qualified published edition close the gap without a new agent?
What independent checker prevents the specialist from self-certifying?

candidate_classes.trigger: new cuneiform reading, translation, royal-inscription interpretation, or campaign synthesis
new stratigraphic, destruction, site-formation, or event-linkage inference
new Tel Dan or related inscription reading, restoration, transliteration, or translation
new Pilate inscription restoration, Latin reading, or title inference
P66 transcription, textual variant, dating, or preferred-reading inference
new original-language alignment or translation judgment
new laboratory result, calibration, or chronological synthesis
Egyptian, Babylonian, Canaanite, Persian, Greek, or Roman religious context is interpreted
Jewish movement, mystical, legal, sectarian, or teacher-development claim is introduced
a doctrine genealogy or tradition-scoped interpretation is introduced
Platonic, Aristotelian, Stoic, or other conceptual lineage is claimed
an apologetics-science interface makes a domain-science claim

risk_routing.low: deterministic validation plus one independent checker
risk_routing.medium: two independent relevant checkers and explicit dissent metadata
risk_routing.high: stop and route evidence packet to human; qualified-domain review may be required
risk_routing.critical: fail closed; no publication or promotion
